activity: Worked with school staff to establish programs with an admissions method that promotes academic diversity
description: The DOE worked with school staff to establish programs with an admissions method that reserves seats for students in low, middle, and high ELA categories, to promote academic diversity through the Educational Option (Ed Opt) admissions method. Some of these programs were previously Screened and Limited Unscreened. These admissions method changes were included in the 2018 New York City High School Directory.
category: Simplifying Admissions Methods and Processes

activity: Encourage the recruitment and retention of men of color to teach in New York City schools
description: In partnership with the Mayor's Young Men's Initiative, the City University of New York, and Teach for America, the DOE engaged in initiatives and programs aiming to put an additional 1,000 men of color on course to become NYC public school teachers by 2018. These initiatives include: building out principal and mentor networks, developing partnerships with universities, charter schools, CBOs (such as ExpandED and EdRising), engaging potential candidates earlier including current high school students, improving the onboarding process by providing convenient training and certification support, improving the hiring process through partial certification exam reimbursement, school tours, virtual interviews, improving professional development opportunities, and utilizing culturally relevant professional and leadership workshops.
category: Fostering Welcoming School Climates for All Students

activity: Participate in NYC Career and Technical Education (CTE) Gender Equity Committee
description: The DOE continues to participate in meetings of the NYC CTE Gender Equity Committee, which meets three times a year. In 2016, the committee focused on recruitment, retention, and engagement. The Committee advised the DOE to specifically focus on educating and engaging middle school guidance counselors. DOE responded to the advice, executed on the advice, and developed four online gender equity modules, targeting counselors.
category: Increasing Participation of Underrepresented Students in STEM and Other Rigorous Courses

activity: Expansion of ASD Horizon program
description: ASD Horizon programs serve students on the autism spectrum whose academic abilities are approaching or are below grade level and who may benefit from instructional and interpersonal supports grounded in the principles of Applied Behavior Analysis. During 2016-17, 69 ASD Horizon programs served students citywide. In 2017-18, 11 new sections will be opened, resulting in a total of 80 ASD Horizon programs citywide.
category: Planning for Diversity When Opening New Schools and Programs

activity: Utilized Pre-K for All providers in raising family awareness about the Kindergarten and Gifted & Talented application processes
description: With the large increase in students enrolled in full-day pre-Kindergarten, the DOE utilized communication with Pre-K for All providers to encourage participation in the Kindergarten and Gifted & Talented admissions processes. This communication included directory distribution, targeted emails about process events, and the sharing of site-level data on student participation.
category: Streamlining and increasing access for families to learn about school options and apply

activity: Gender Equity Trainings made available
description: Gender Equity Coordinator, Kimberly Shannon, offered Gender Equity in Schools trainings throughout the year. She has trained all Single Shepherds, as well as some parent coordinators, school staff, and parents.
category: Fostering Welcoming School Climates for All Students

activity: Dual language programs available on Kindergarten & pre-Kindergarten applications
description: As part of the central pre-K and Kindergarten applications, families are allowed to apply directly to Dual Language program offerings rather than just the school itself. This allows families to express a preference for this type of pedagogy, as well as enable the DOE to better anticipate incoming populations of English Language Learners. On this application families were asked three short questions to identify potential ELLs.
category: Streamlining and increasing access for families to learn about school options and apply

activity: Expanded Dual Language programs
description: The DOE continued to support schools in expanding and opening new Dual Language programs. For the 2016-17 school year, the DOE offered 469 bilingual programs across the city, including 182 Dual Language programs. During the 2017-18 school year, the DOE plans to open 72 new bilingual programs, 38 of which are Dual Language programs. Overall in the 2017-18 school year, the DOE will offer approximately 500 bilingual programs across the city, including approximately 200 Dual Language programs.
category: Planning for Diversity When Opening New Schools and Programs

activity: NYSED Socioeconomic Integration Pilot Program - Brooklyn STEAM Center
description: The Brooklyn Navy Yard serves as the cooperative service and technical hub (the Brooklyn STEAM Center) for high-quality Career and Technical Education programs serving students from a range of socioeconomic backgrounds in Brooklyn. The Brooklyn STEAM Center is a NYSED grant funded program aimed at providing socioeconomic diversity for all students and schools within the pilot. This program opened in Fall 2015 and will continue to expand into 2017-18.
category: Increasing Participation of Underrepresented Students in STEM and Other Rigorous Courses

activity: Equity & Excellence - District- Charter Partnerships
description: District-Charter Partnerships pairs district and charter schools to foster strong relationships and share best practices. In 2016-17, 37 schools participated in school-to-school district-charter partnerships. In 2017-18, over 120 district and charter schools will be partnering around sharing best practices, including co-located schools building campus community and sharing practices, collaborative learning partnerships through the District-Charter Collaborative, the KIPP Through College Summer Bridge program, and training through the DOE Uncommon Schools-Impact Partnership. In addition, several community and high school superintendents are working to implement district-wide partnerships throughout the year.
category: Equity & Excellence for All

activity: Opened Round 2 early
description: To give families the maximum amount of time in which to apply, the DOE opened the Round 2 application three weeks ahead of schedule and did not change the planned close date.
category: Streamlining and increasing access for families to learn about school options and apply

activity: Outreach and information sharing with students with accessibility needs
description: The DOE conducts outreach to families of pre-Kindergarten and Kindergarten students with accessibility needs to inform them of the two processes they can leverage to obtain an accessible site for their child. Additionally, the DOE developed a brochure for students with accessibility needs to support their navigation of the admissions processes.
category: Streamlining and increasing access for families to learn about school options and apply

activity: Equity & Excellence - Universal Literacy
description: Through Universal Literacy, schools receive support from a dedicated reading coach, who works with Kindergarten through 2nd grade teachers to ensure students are reading on grade level by the end of 2nd grade. The goal of the initiative is to have at least two-thirds of students reading proficiently by the end of 2nd grade by 2022, with the target of 100 percent of all 2nd-graders reading at grade level by 2026. In 2016-17, 100 teachers were hired and trained to become reading coaches in four districts. As of fall 2017, 242 Universal Literacy reading coaches are supporting all 305 elementary schools serving approximately 75,000 kindergarten through 2nd graders across 14 districts, including all districts in the Bronx.
category: Equity & Excellence for All

activity: DREAM-SHSI - Implemented Specialized High Schools alumni support for first time
description: DREAM-SHSI is an extracurricular program of rigorous coursework designed to assist economically disadvantaged NYC students in preparing for the Specialized High Schools Admissions Test (SHSAT). There are two DREAM programs: the Specialized High School Institute (DREAM-SHSI), which runs from the middle of grade 6 to the fall of grade 8, and the Summer/Fall Intensive, which runs during the summer and fall before students plan to take the SHSAT. All participating middle school students in DREAM-SHSI heard from and spoke to teams of recent Specialized High Schools (SHS) alumni about transitioning and persisting in SHS during three sessions in spring 2017. During the final session, parents of participating students were invited to join the alumni for an informational session about SHS.
category: Improving Diversity at the Specialized High Schools

activity: Established School Diversity Advisory Group to support diverse and inclusive schools and programs
description: In June 2017, as part of the diversity plan, the DOE established a School Diversity Advisory Group, which will make formal policy recommendations to the Mayor and Chancellor, and a process for engaging community school districts in planning around diversity. The chairs of the Advisory Group are José Calderón, President of the Hispanic Federation, Maya Wiley, chair of the Civilian Complaint Review Board and Professor of Urban Policy and Management at the New School, and Hazel Dukes, President of the NAACP New York State Conference. The Advisory Group will also include city government stakeholders, local and national experts on school diversity, parents, advocates, students, and other community leaders.
category: Equity & Excellence for All

activity: Released Transgender and Gender Nonconforming Student Guidelines
description: The DOE released updated Transgender and Gender Nonconforming Student Guidelines, which included  expanded definitions, updated language, clarification of student records policies, and more. The DOE developed guidance based on this to support schools and families as they engaged in admissions and enrollment processes.
target_population: Families of LGBT students, schools, and communities
category: Fostering Welcoming School Climates for All Students

activity: Finalized plans to align admissions processes for 3-K, pre-K, and Kindergarten
description: The DOE developed plans to switch from a "Round 1/Round 2" model for the pre-K application and a "Main Round/Waitlist" model for 3-K to a "Main Round/Late Application" process for both for fall 2018 admissions, which will bring them into alignment with the Kindergarten application. This greatly simplifies the application process for families participating in successive years' admissions processes.
category: Simplifying Admissions Methods and Processes

activity: Updated regulations to support students in temporary housing and foster care
description: The DOE amended Chancellor's Regulation A-101 in January 2017 to include additional protections for students in temporary housing and students in foster care, and to implement the requirements of the Every Student Succeeds Act (ESSA).
category: Improving Efforts to Support Students in Temporary Housing

activity: Convened stakeholders to discuss ways to support LGBTQ youth of color
description: In November 2016, the NYC Men Teach program, the Expanded Success Initiative, and the City University of New York, in partnership with the White House Initiative on Educational Excellence for African Americans and the Hetrick-Martin Institute, convened students, teacher-leaders, administrators, and community leaders to participate in a community forum on supporting LGBTQ youth of color in our school communities.
category: Fostering Welcoming School Climates for All Students

activity: Expansion of Bilingual Special Education programs
description: Bilingual Special Education (BSE) programs serve students who need a special class or Integrated Co-Teaching classroom with instruction in English and another language. In 2016-17, 202 BSE programs served students citywide. During 2017-18, 28 new sections will be opened, resulting in a total of 230 BSE programs citywide.
category: Planning for Diversity When Opening New Schools and Programs

activity: Supported professional development and learning opportunities focused on LGBT experiences
description: Through the Lambda Literary Writers and Schools program, the DOE seeks to pair teachers with LGBT authors, provides copies of the author's book, and brings the author into the classroom. In 2016-17, the program was expanded to 40 schools.
category: Fostering Welcoming School Climates for All Students

activity: Appointed Kimberly Shannon as DOE’s first Gender Equity Coordinator
description: Kimberly Shannon was appointed to be the DOE’s first Gender Equity Coordinator in December 2016. Housed within the Office of Counseling Support Programs, Shannon's role was initially funded by the City Council, and has since been baselined by the DOE.
category: Fostering Welcoming School Climates for All Students

activity: Translation of teacher and principal rating information materials in 9 DOE languages
description: Teacher and principal evaluation rating information sheets continue to be translated into the nine official DOE languages in order to reach parents and legal guardians of students in the DOE school system who are not native-English speakers. This allows non-native English speaking parents and legal guardians the same access to these material as their native English-speaking counterparts.
category: Streamlining and Increasing Access for families to learn about school options and apply

activity: Launched 3-K programs in districts 7 and 23
description: 3-K for All brings free, full-day, high-quality education to 3-year-olds in NYC. In June 2017, the DOE began the path to 3-K for All in districts 7 and 23 by launching the first 3-K application process for fall 2017 admissions. In 2017-18, the DOE will be expanding to two additional school districts for fall 2018 admissions.
category: Equity & Excellence for All

activity: Plan to develop targeted interventions for families of Students in Temporary Housing (STH) and English Language Learners (ELL)
description: The DOE has partnered with social policy research organization, MDRC, to design and test interventions to improve access to Kindergarten options and to improve the application process for ELL  and STH families in order to inform future practice.
target_population: English Language Learners, Students in Temporary Housing
category: Improving Efforts to Support Students in Temporary Housing

activity: Allowed school schedule flexibility and encouraged sharing of best practices to support diverse school communities
description: As part of Progressive Redesign Opportunity Schools for Excellence (PROSE), schools are allowed flexibility in how their school day is organized and encouraged to implement models of teacher inter-visitation, with many schools centering this work on the goal of meeting the needs of a diverse student body. In 2016-17, 79 schools participated in schedule flexibility, allowing leaders to tailor school structure to meet specific needs of school communities. Many schools have implemented teacher inter-visitations, encouraging the sharing of best practices in how to most effectively serve a diverse school community. Last year’s survey results show that of the schools surveyed, 76% feel that the scheduling flexibility created more opportunities for teachers to collaborate. Other benefits include: increased instructional time for students, additional time for parent engagement, and more opportunities for student advisory support.
category: Targeting Funding to Foster Diversity

activity: Moved toward eliminating revealed middle school ranking
description: In 2016-17, all middle schools in District 15 implemented "blind ranking" for the middle school admissions process, which meant that middle schools would no longer be able to see where a student ranked them on their application. For the 2017-18 school year, districts 4, 5, 13 and 14 will also implement blind ranking. The remaining districts (1, 2, 3) will implement blind ranking for the 2018-19 school year. Blind ranking for all screened middle schools will create a more equitable process and help foster more diverse classes of qualified students by enabling families to apply to schools in their true preference order, as opposed to in a strategic manner. The DOE has been conducting trainings to support middle schools affected by this change and communicating this update to families.
category: Increasing Access to Screened Schools

activity: Implemented re-zoning with a focus on diversity
description: The DOE proposed and CEC 13 approved an elementary school re-zoning in Brooklyn Heights/DUMBO/Vinegar Hill, shifting the zone lines between P.S. 8 and P.S. 307 for implementation in the 2016-17 school year. One of the goals of the rezoning was to create a more diverse P.S. 307 zone to be more aligned with the neighborhood by equalizing the demographics of P.S. 307’s zone with P.S. 8’s zone. The re-zoning resulted in less socioeconomic and racial isolation in each school's zone.
category: Ensuring Diversity is a Factor in School Rezoning

activity: Equity & Excellence - Algebra for All
description: Through Algebra for All, by 2022, every student will have access to Algebra in 8th grade, complete Algebra no later than 9th grade, and there will be academic supports in place in elementary and middle school to build greater Algebra readiness. As of fall 2017, approximately 900 teachers across 357 elementary, middle, and high schools have received Algebra for All training to strengthen math instruction and are working to increase the amount of time they devote to math instruction. 139 elementary schools are working to “departmentalize” 5th-grade math – having their math instruction led by a specialized teacher who has received intensive training.
category: Equity & Excellence for All

activity: Created first alumni mentoring programs
description: As its first efforts to connect former and current NYC public school students, the DOE created two alumni mentoring programs to provide one-on-one mentoring for high-needs high school students from lower-income backgrounds and lower-performing schools, and students of color. The programs emphasize college and career readiness and include alumni-led college tours and college application workshops.
category: Equity & Excellence for All

activity: Provided grant funding for schools to increase school diversity through recruitment & support of diverse learners
description: The Progressive Redesign Opportunity Schools for Excellence (PROSE) used funding from the National Education Association to provide $750 mini-grants and an opportunity to apply for up to $5,000 in mini-grant funding to 10 schools who sought to increase diversity in their school communities. Many of these schools utilized this funding to provide planning time for school staff working on diversity issues, as well as to do additional recruitment and outreach to underrepresented populations through school fairs and direct communication to families. Additionally, schools also utilized this funding to better equip their schools to support diverse learners. Examples of these activities included full-day professional development and guest speakers. Of the 155 schools in the program, 10 schools received grants of up to $5,000 for this effort.
category: Targeting Funding to Foster Diversity

activity: Announced Single Stall Bathroom Initiative
description: The DOE has committed to making sure every school building has a single stall bathroom available to support the privacy needs of students, including those with medical conditions and disabilities, as well as transgender and gender non-conforming students. Schools are supported with making sure the lock is accessible and signage is consistent across all schools. The DOE began implementation of this in the 2016-17 school year and will continue until all schools have a single stall bathroom.
category: Fostering Welcoming School Climates for All Students

activity: NYSED Socioeconomic Integration Pilot Program - District 9
description: The purpose of the Socioeconomic Integration Pilot Program is to increase student achievement in select high poverty Priority and Focus Schools by encouraging greater socioeconomic integration or by decreasing socioeconomic isolation in these schools. Through this program, District 9 developed its innovative, project-based, Science, Technology, Engineering and Math (STEM) programs  and curricula in 2016-17. District 9 will continue to work with I.S. 117 Joseph H. Wade and Bronx Writing Academy, which are partnering with elementary and middle schools serving higher-income populations in districts 9 and 10 in the implementation of STEM activities.
category: Increasing Participation of Underrepresented Students in STEM and Other Rigorous Courses

activity: Gender Inclusive Schools Capacity Building Training
description: The DOE offered a full-day training through partnership with the Hetrick-Martin Institute. The training covered transgender terminology, DOE policies, and gave participants an opportunity to practice knowledge via role plays and case studies. 534 staff attended in 2016-17.
category: Fostering Welcoming School Climates for All Students

activity: Implemented diversity in admissions pilots across all grade levels, pre-Kindergarten through High School
description: As a result of the formal call for proposals, for the 2016-17 school year, 19 diversity in admissions pilots were implemented, including 12 elementary schools, 1 Gifted & Talented school, 4 middle schools, and 2 high schools. Applications continue to be submitted by schools on a rolling basis for consideration for the 2018-19 school year. In addition, New York City Early Education Centers (NYCEECs) have been engaged to submit proposals for the first time.
category: Expanding Diversity in Admissions Pilots

activity: Built a new easy-to-use online tool that lets users search New York City’s hundreds of high school choices by school name, keyword, location, size, and more
description: NYC School Finder, developed by the DOE’s Office of Student Enrollment and Division of Instructional and Information Technology in collaboration with the Mayor’s Office of Technology & Innovation and Pivotal Labs, was first released in September 2016. School Finder was built to help families address the challenges of the City’s high school admissions process and identify 12 choices for their high school application, and is currently available in Spanish and English. In addition to English and Spanish, School Finder will be available in Arabic, Bengali, Chinese, French, Haitian Creole, Korean, Russian, and Urdu in fall 2017.
category: Streamlining and increasing access for families to learn about school options and apply

activity: Specialized High Schools Diversity Initiative - Expand DREAM, a SHSAT preparation program, to serve additional rising 8th grade students in an Intensive program
description: DREAM-SHSI is an extracurricular program of rigorous coursework designed to assist economically disadvantaged NYC students in preparing for the Specialized High Schools Admissions Test (SHSAT). There are two DREAM programs: the Specialized High School Institute (DREAM-SHSI), which runs from the middle of grade 6 to the fall of grade 8, and the Summer/Fall Intensive, which runs during the summer and fall before students plan to take the SHSAT. In summer 2016, the DOE implemented the Summer/Fall Intensive for the first time, targeting the highest-performing rising 8th graders from underrepresented districts. DREAM participants who took the fall 2016 SHSAT comprised 6 percent of Black and Latino testers, but 26 percent of Black and Latino SHSAT students who received Specialized High School offers.
target_population: High performing, economically disadvantaged middle school students (22-month DREAM program) and high performing rising 8th graders from underrepresented districts (DREAM Intensive)
category: Improving Diversity at the Specialized High Schools

activity: Citywide Career and Technical Education (CTE) High School Fair
description: The second annual Citywide CTE High School fair showcased industry and college partners collaborating with CTE programs in addition to a panel on "Bright Futures: Girls in CTE”. The Special Education Office and DOE's Translations Team were in attendance with resources to support middle school families. The “Bright Futures: Girls in CTE” panel event was aimed at middle school students and their parents/guardians. The goal was to educate and inform parents, guardians and our students about the various options, both in college and careers, that open up for CTE students, especially in fields where women are underrepresented.
category: Increasing Participation of Underrepresented Students in STEM and Other Rigorous Courses

activity: Equity & Excellence - College Access for All High School
description: By the 2018-19 school year, every student will have the resources and supports at their high school to graduate with an individual college and career plan. In 2016-17, 101 schools received training and funding to build a schoolwide college and career culture; additionally, the City eliminated the CUNY college application fee for low-income students and made the SAT exam available free of charge during the school day for all high school juniors. Currently, 269 high schools are receiving training and funding to build a schoolwide college and career culture.
category: Equity & Excellence for All

activity: Specialized High Schools Diversity Initiative - Expand Discovery, a preparation program for disadvantaged rising 9th graders
description: In summer 2017, seven Specialized High Schools hosted a Discovery Program to give disadvantaged NYC students with demonstrated high potential the opportunity to gain admission. For the first time in several years, the Bronx High School of Science hosted a Discovery Program. Across the seven schools, over 200 students were served. In spring 2018, Stuyvesant High School will also prepare to launch a program, at which point all testing Specialized High Schools will participate in the Discovery program.
category: Improving Diversity at the Specialized High Schools

activity: Continued programs to mentor and support Students in Temporary Housing (STH)
description: The OBAMA, SIMBA, and ASET programs provide mentoring and support services to male and female students in temporary housing. They focus on identifying and supporting students who are English Language Learners, newcomers, and/or LGBTQ. The programs allow for a safe space for these students to thrive and build around their “common differences". The programs also encourage a college-going culture through college tours, which encourages school persistence and college-readiness.
category: Improving Efforts to Support Students in Temporary Housing

activity: Prioritized Renewal School students for summer STEM and additional enrichment programs
description: Students attending Renewal Schools in the 2016-17 school year were given priority enrollment in DOE Summer STEM programs for summer 2017. Renewal Schools also created additional summer enrichment programs for their students including a Summer Bridge program, SAT Prep, and CareerCLUE. Greater access to enrichment programs encouraged program diversity and combatted summer learning loss among students. Summer sites were added in Districts 9 and 27.
category: Increasing Participation of Underrepresented Students in STEM and Other Rigorous Courses

activity: Issued policy statement to facilitate more diverse and inclusive schools and programs
description: In June 2017, as part of the diversity plan, the DOE issued a policy statement identifying its commitment to school diversity and belief that all students benefit from diverse and inclusive classrooms. This statement provides a platform for the DOE to implement its vision of Equity and Excellence for all NYC students with a focus on diversity and inclusion.
category: Equity & Excellence for All

activity: Provided accessibility information for testing sites.
description: In 2016-17, families continued to have the opportunity to select testing sites that met their accessibility needs.
category: Increasing Access to Screened Schools

activity: Foster equity-focused conversations and programs in school communities
description: Through the Expanded Success Initiative (ESI), the DOE facilitated monthly open forums with school leaders, students, and community members to unpack issues related to race, gender and class. It also hosted a peer-to-peer mentorship program, serving primarily young men of color, aimed at engaging students from underserved communities in a college and career readiness mindset. Additionally, in partnership with the Center for Strategic Solutions at NYU, ESI hosted a Critically Conscious Educators Rising (CCER) Series that convened a group of like-minded educators to focus on tying theory to practice in the pursuit of equity and racial justice in their classrooms, through their peers, and beyond. Through the ESI Leadership Institute, the DOE hosted a four-part collaborative series bringing together principals and assistant principals to explore systematic bias and racism in schools and what building leaders can do to disrupt it. Administrators and leaders from over 30 schools have come together to learn how to create a roadmap towards an equity-driven school community using data and guided by a root cause analysis process.
category: Fostering Welcoming School Climates for All Students

activity: Implemented 3rd Grade G&T programs that utilized multiple measures of assessing giftedness
description: Five new 3rd grade Gifted & Talented programs were offered in Districts 3, 7, 12, 16 and 23 that utilized multiple measures of achievement to identify eligible students. These measures included student grades, state test scores, and teacher recommendations. All students residing in these districts were eligible for consideration. The students enrolled in these programs were largely more reflective of their district population, contributing to the diversity of G&T enrollment overall.
category: Increasing Access to Screened Schools

activity: Continued participation in the LGBT+ Advisory Council
description: The LGBT+ Advisory Council met regularly with 34 community organizations and other city agencies. Members reviewed policies, created best practices, and collaboratively planned to better support LGBT issues in schools.
category: Fostering Welcoming School Climates for All Students

activity: NYSED Socioeconomic Integration Pilot Program - District 13
description: The D13 SIPP grant working group continues its planning and implementation work which includes creating a magnet program at MS 113, proposing a permissible, educationally sound, equitable districtwide choice-based socioeconomic integration policy and developing a family resource center.
category: Targeting Funding to Foster Diversity

activity: NYSED Socioeconomic Integration Pilot Program - District 3
description: The purpose of the Socioeconomic Integration Pilot Program is to increase student achievement in select high poverty Priority and Focus Schools by encouraging greater socioeconomic integration or by decreasing socioeconomic isolation in these schools. Through this program, District 3 developed its innovative, project-based, Science, Technology, Engineering and Math (STEM) programs in 2016-17. District 3 will continue to work with Frederick Douglass Academy II Secondary School, which is partnering with elementary and middle schools serving higher-income populations in district 3 in the implementation of STEM activities in the 2017-18 school year.
category: Increasing Participation of Underrepresented Students in STEM and Other Rigorous Courses

activity: Equity & Excellence - Single Shepherd
description: Single Shepherd is pairing every student in grades 6-12 in District 7 in the South Bronx and District 23 in Brownsville with a dedicated school counselor or social worker who will support them in their school on the path to graduation and college enrollment. Approximately 140 Single Shepherds are serving approximately 15,000 grade 6-12 students at all 49 middle and high schools in Districts 7 and 23.
category: Equity & Excellence for All

activity: Provided additional supports for students in temporary housing to participate in 3K-High School admissions processes
description: Supports and interventions have been put into place to increase awareness of and access to 3K through High School admissions processes for students in temporary housing and their families. These interventions have included transportation provided to admissions events, admissions hubs for students at fairs, trainings for shelter staff, shelter-based workshops, direct outreach to pre-Kindergarten non-applicants and other opportunities for targeted admissions support. In the 2016-17 admissions cycle, 41 percent of eligible students in shelter applied for Kindergarten, up from 36 the previous year. 32 percent of 8th graders in shelter listed 12 choices on their high school application – up from 27 percent the previous year, and higher than the citywide average. In 2017-18, the DOE will expand the number of admissions hubs and offer targeted shelter-based events.
category: Improving Efforts to Support Students in Temporary Housing

activity: School redesign and new school creation to respond to student and community needs
description: The DOE works with Superintendents to collaborate with each school community - staff, parents, students, and other community stakeholders- to respond to educational needs, particularly when schools are exhibiting declining academic performance. The range of redesign strategies include: Addition of new programs or services (School Redesign),  New School development, School relocation (Resiting), Grade reconfiguration (Truncation / Expansion), Consolidation and Closure. The end result is a better option for students, one whose culture reflects a single cohesive community and a higher instructional quality which leads to student achievement. These strategies are constructed with potential impacts on school diversity in mind.
category: Planning for Diversity When Opening New Schools and Programs

activity: Specialized High Schools Diversity Initiative - Leverage existing middle school after school programs to implement new Specialized High School Admissions Test preparation programs
description: In 2016-17, the DOE launched ~50 middle school Specialized High School Admissions Test (SHSAT) preparation programs, using 2 models. 1) A Capacity Building Initiative, which trained middle school teachers on the content, skills, and best pedagogical practices for teaching SHSAT preparation. ~30 schools in targeted underrepresented districts sent teachers to these trainings in January and April 2017, and were then provided with SHSAT prep materials for their students and budget allocations to pay teachers to lead prep classes for 7th graders in the spring of 2017. 2) In collaboration with the Department of Youth & Community Development, the DOE contracted with nine private test preparation vendors to offer SHSAT test preparation courses at ~20 afterschool programs in underrepresented districts in the spring of 2018.
target_population: Middle school students from underrepresented districts
category: Improving Diversity at the Specialized High Schools

activity: Eased the High School Admissions appeals process for high-needs students
description: In 2016-17, the DOE improved the High School admissions appeals process for (1) students in temporary housing or foster care who moved or were expecting to move and (2) students requiring a different High School as a result of their gender identity, including transgender students who were transitioning. These students were able to submit formal appeals through the HS admissions process and thereby obtain new High School offers before the end of their 8th grade year.
target_population: Students in Temporary Housing and Transgender students
category: Simplifying Admissions Methods and Processes

activity: Provided ~40 professional development opportunities for staff in all five boroughs on LGBTQ identity
description: The LGBT Community Liaison, Jared Fox, conducted 39 professional development (PD) sessions reaching a total of ~1,900 individuals. Each PD session covered LGBT terminology and best practices. These sessions were at various all-staff PD sessions, superintendent meetings, as well as parent coordinator sessions.
category: Fostering Welcoming School Climates for All Students

activity: Display seat targets and demand information for both General Education and Students with Disabilities in 2018 New York City Middle and High School Directories
description: All middle and high schools that participate in the DOE's centralized admissions process have seats allocated for Students with Disabilities (SWDs). This enrollment target is set in proportion to the overall percent of SWDs by borough (for High School) and by district (for Middle School). In the annual school directories, the DOE continued to provide information about seat availability and prior-year demand for each program for General Education and SWDs separately in order to highlight the fact that all schools serve SWDs.
category: Increasing Access to Screened Schools

activity: Translation of handbooks and directories in 10 languages
description: For PK-12 admissions processes, translated directories were distributed to schools, DOE offices, and community based organizations for each admissions process. Quantities of translations were customized using the available home language data by district or borough. All directories were also available online.
target_population: English Language Learners and families with non-English home language
category: Streamlining and increasing access for families to learn about school options and apply

activity: Conducted additional outreach to populations that have participated in Gifted & Talented at lower rates than students citywide
description: In addition to standard modes of outreach, OSE sent a postcard highlighting the opportunity to test for Gifted & Talented to all students citywide entering kindergarten who were eligible to take the test . The Committees on Preschool Special Education (CPSEs) also conducted additional outreach to students participating in the Turning 5 process.
category: Increasing Access to Screened Schools

activity: Continuation of Federal Magnet school programs
description: The primary purpose of magnet schools as defined in federal legislation is to assist in the desegregation of schools. In the federal Magnet Schools Assistance Program for 2016-17, the DOE implemented magnet programs at 26 elementary, PK-8 and middle schools across 11 districts. This includes magnet programs that have been in place in Districts 13, 15 and 28 since 2013, and magnets in Districts 14, 21, 22, 25, 27, 29, 30 and 32 that launched in the fall of 2016. Magnet schools offer a wide range of distinctive education programs and partnerships capable of attracting substantial numbers of students of different backgrounds.  In addition to the programs that were in place in 2016-17, the DOE received three new magnet grants for Queens, Manhattan and Bronx districts that will begin in October 2017.
category: Targeting funding to foster diversity

activity: Enabled pre-K providers to operate blended EarlyLearn and DOE funded classes
description: Blended classrooms are an opportunity for pre-K programs that operate with an ACS EarlyLearn contract and a DOE pre-K contract to serve these students in one classroom. This policy allows students who meet eligibility requirements based on income (EarlyLearn) and students who may not (DOE) to learn together. Three programs participated in 2016-17.
category: Planning for Diversity When Opening New Schools and Programs

activity: Equity & Excellence - College Access for All Middle School
description: By the 2018-19 school year, every middle school student will have the opportunity to visit a college campus. In 2016-17, 171 schools across 11 districts implemented the program. In 2017-18, 355 middle schools across 22 districts will bring approximately 43,000 7th-graders to college campuses, and engage students and families in a schoolwide college and career culture.
category: Equity & Excellence for All

activity: Encouraged schools with school-based admissions to set targets for admitting students with disabilities
description: The DOE continued to support middle schools in recruiting and supporting students with disabilities, including middle schools that currently serve lower numbers of students with disabilities.
category: Increasing Access to Screened Schools

activity: Encouraged Students in Temporary Housing (STH) to take the Gifted and Talented (G&T) and Specialized High Schools Admission (SHSAT) tests.
description: The DOE conducted outreach throughout the five boroughs to encourage STH to test for G&T Programs and the Specialized High Schools (SHS). Students were taken on tours of the Specialized High Schools in their respective boroughs to motivate students and expose them to SHS environments. Direct outreach and application collection was conducted at shelters for students interested in taking the G&T test.
category: Improving Efforts to Support Students in Temporary Housing

activity: Hosted conferences to support non-English speaking families
description: The DOE hosted seven native language conferences in 2016-17 in Spanish, Mandarin, Bengali and Arabic for parents and their children. The conferences were held entirely in the families' native language and gave parents tools and strategies for supporting their children in school and life, as well as information about DOE and city services. The conference also included a "Know Your Rights" panel discussion in collaboration with the Mayor's Office of Immigrant Affairs.
category: Fostering Welcoming School Climates for All Students

activity: Work with schools to streamline school tours, open houses, and registration for school-based assessments and auditions
description: In order to help alleviate some of the anxiety, time and resources families expend on attending school tours, open houses, and school-based assessments, the DOE is working with schools to collect and display all open house and school tour information on the DOE website. In 2016-17, the DOE published a spring open house calendar for High School admissions, in addition to the fall calendar. The DOE also publishes a fall calendar for middle school. The DOE continues to work with schools toward simplifying school-based assessments and optimizing their recruitment strategies.
category: Streamlining and increasing access for families to learn about school options and apply

activity: Produced offers for all Pre-Kindergarten aged students in shelter
description: In spring 2017, all four-year-olds in shelter who had not applied to Pre-K received an offer to a free, full-day, high-quality Pre-K for All program. In partnership with the Department of Homeless Services (DHS), the DOE conducted continued outreach to these families to ensure they were aware of their offer.
category: Improving Efforts to Support Students in Temporary Housing

activity: Equity & Excellence - Computer Science for All
description: Through Computer Science for All, every student will receive computer science education in elementary, middle, and high school by 2025. By 2016-17, approximately 940 teachers received Computer Science for All training to bring back to their 524 elementary, middle, and high schools.
category: Equity & Excellence for All

activity: Provided simultaneous interpretation, translated materials, and other interpretation services at all Student Enrollment events
description: For all DOE admissions events where a formal presentation was given, simultaneous interpretation services were available, based on the language population of the district or borough. Additionally, all events received translated signage and materials, as well as the services of interpreters to work with families one-on-one.
target_population: English Language Learners and families with non-English home language
category: Streamlining and increasing access for families to learn about school options and apply

activity: Application and Test Registrations (RFT) available in 10 languages
description: Applications for all elementary admissions processes were available on paper and online in 10 languages. Applications and request for testing for middle school and high school admissions processes were available on paper in 10 languages.
target_population: English Language Learners and families with non-English home language
category: Streamlining and increasing access for families to learn about school options and apply

activity: Women's History Month celebrated in schools & DOE Central Offices
description: During the month of March, the DOE hosted its first American Women's History Panel, featuring experts in American Women's History who discussed the opportunities and challenges in making K-12 curriculum more inclusive of American women's history. Teachers, Central staff, and Field Support staff were present for this event. Posters were also sent to all Respect for All liaisons, who are staff members who serve as resources for students and staff on issues of discrimination, harassment, intimidation, and/or bullying, to recognize historical female figures.
category: Fostering Welcoming School Climates for All Students

activity: Community School District 1 SIPP Grant and Diversity in Admissions Plan established
description: In collaboration with the District 1 Community Education Council and the District 1 Community School Superintendent's Office, the DOE is piloting a district-wide diversity in admission plan for the 2017-18 pre-Kindergarten and Kindergarten admissions cycle (for the entering class of fall 2018). In addition, a Family Resource Center was established in fall 2017 and serves as a one-stop shop for families to learn about and enroll in District 1 schools.
category: Expanding Diversity in Admissions Pilots

activity: Specialized High Schools Diversity Initiative - Developed an outreach team aimed at increasing  SHS enrollment among underrepresented populations
description: In 2016-17, the DOE formed a team of outreach specialists focused on raising awareness about the Specialized High Schools (SHS). The team called thousands of families, attended more than 20 events, and presented about the SHS at ~25 middle schools in underrepresented districts (Districts 4-6 in Manhattan, Districts 7-12 in the Bronx, and Districts 16-19, 23 and 32 in Brooklyn).  In spring 2017, the DOE hosted inaugural SHS fairs in Brooklyn and the Bronx with the goal of increasing awareness about the SHS in communities that are underrepresented at the schools. ~5,000 people attended across both events. In 2017-18, the outreach team will continue to build upon this work by strengthening relationships with community partners with the goal of effectively promoting and increasing visibility of the SHS to students and families from underrepresented backgrounds.
category: Improving Diversity at the Specialized High Schools

activity: Expanded programs for English Language Learners in District 75
description: In 2016-17, there were a total of 47 bilingual in District 75 programs. Included in these are a new Chinese Transitional Bilingual Education (TBE) program, a middle school TBE Spanish Program, and a middle school TBE Yiddish Program. For the 2017-18 school year, there will be a total of 49 bilingual programs.
category: Planning for Diversity When Opening New Schools and Programs

activity: Brought together schools working on diversity initiatives to share ideas
description: During three professional development sessions, Progressive Redesign Opportunity Schools for Excellence (PROSE) brought principals and teachers within 32 schools together to discuss the implementation practices/challenges of their diversity plans. Topics discussed included recruitment strategies, tracking student data, professional development, and parent outreach. Ten schools were awarded $5,000 mini-grants in support of their diversity implementation efforts.
category: Targeting Funding to Foster Diversity

activity: Expanded work-based learning opportunities for underrepresented students
description: In 2016-17, the DOE was awarded funding from City Council's Young Women's Initiative to expand work-based learning opportunities. Using this funding, the DOE launched a Career Mentoring in Construction program and a Career Mentoring in Architecture and Engineering program. Both programs had retention rates of 99% and recruited and engaged underrepresented student populations in these Career and Technical Education clusters. For 2017-18, the DOE will expand the reach of these initiatives.
category: Increasing Participation of Underrepresented Students in STEM and Other Rigorous Courses

activity: Began to eliminate "limited unscreened" as a high school admissions method and replace with admissions method that will promote greater diversity
description: As part of the DOE's diversity plan,  the Limited Unscreened admissions method will be removed beginning with the 2018-19 admissions cycle, as it creates barriers to entry for families. For fall 2017 admissions, there were 245 high school programs and 94 middle schools using this admissions method. For fall 2018, 59 programs across 49 schools opted to change their limited unscreened admissions method. The DOE is working with school leaders, school communities, and superintendents to transition all limited unscreened high school programs for students entering high school in fall 2019. The DOE has also partnered with researchers to ensure a thoughtful transition to an admissions method that does not negatively affect any specific student group.
category: Simplifying Admissions Methods and Processes

activity: Expansion of ASD Nest program
description: ASD Nest programs serve students with autism whose academic abilities are on grade-level and whose primary need for support is in the areas of language and social skill development. During 2016-17, 265 ASD Nest programs served students citywide. In 2017-18, 18 new sections will be opened resulting in a total of 283 ASD Nest programs citywide.
category: Planning for Diversity When Opening New Schools and Programs

activity: Provide curriculum resources to support LGBT students
description: With support from the City Council, the DOE partnered with WNET to create a series of short videos and discussion guides for schools to talk about LGBT identity. They also conducted professional development sessions with teachers to demonstrate how to utilize these resources.
category: Fostering Welcoming School Climates for All Students

activity: Implemented re-zoning with a focus on diversity
description: The DOE worked with CEC 3 to develop a re-zoning impacting most of District 3 and one of the goals was to draw the zone lines in a way that equalized diversity across the zones. The rezoning was approved in 2016-17 for implementation in 2017-18. This re-zoning is generally projected to reduce socioeconomic and racial concentrations in certain schools' zones and distribute students more equitably across the district.
category: Ensuring Diversity is a Factor in School Rezoning

activity: Specialized High Schools Diversity Initiative - Offer the SHSAT during the school day to ease the burden of weekend testing
description: In 2016-17, the DOE offered the Specialized High School Admissions Test (SHSAT) during the school day at 7 middle schools in order to ease the burden of weekend testing. As a result, the number of students testing at those schools increased by more than 50 percent. Each school also offered a free SHSAT preparation program. In 2017-18, the DOE expanded the SHSAT School Day program to a total of 15 middle schools.
category: Improving Diversity at the Specialized High Schools

activity: Streamlined transfer process to ensure English Language Learners gain access to programs that meet their needs
description: The DOE revised the English Language Learner transfer process by formalizing the request process in order to improve outcomes for families. This means schools must submit standard requests with evidence of the need for transfer, and ultimate parent authorization of the placement is required. The new process fosters greater transparency and engagement for families and schools and facilitates reporting to both NYSED and the Department of Justice.
category: Simplifying Admissions Methods and Processes

activity: Equity & Excellence - AP for All
description: AP for All is adding Advanced Placement courses so that by fall 2021, students at all high schools will have access to at least five AP classes. In 2016-17, 120 AP courses were added across 63 schools, 31 of which did not previously offer any AP courses. As of fall 2017, 152 high schools are offering new AP courses, including 60 that offered no AP courses before the initiative. As part of the AP for All initiative, the DOE has partnered with Equal Opportunity Schools as part of the national Lead Higher Initiative to specifically increase AP participation and success at 24 high schools among students of color and low income students who are not currently enrolled in AP courses.
category: Equity & Excellence for All

activity: Trainings in Dating Violence offered to school staff
description: The DOE partnered with the Mayor's Office to Combat Domestic Violence to offer trainings in Dating Violence for school staff, particularly targeting school counselors and Respect for All liaisons, who are staff members who serve as resources for students and staff on issues of discrimination, harassment, intimidation, and/or bullying . These trainings focus on dismantling misperceptions about dating violence, and on highlighting the ways that sexism, racism, and homophobia play into dating violence dynamics. The DOE also leveraged Day One, a non-profit organization focused on preventing dating abuse, to do such trainings. Approximately 250 counselors and social workers were trained in 2016-17. The DOE is aiming to train all Respect for All liaisons by the end of 2019-20.
category: Fostering Welcoming School Climates for All Students

activity: Pride celebrated in schools & DOE Central Offices
description: The DOE continued to hold Pride Celebration, honoring students, families, and staff who are creating LGBT inclusive environments. The DOE marched in Queens and Brooklyn Pride marches and had a float for the Manhattan Heritage of Pride March. The DOE marching contingent in Queens was awarded "Simply the Best" marching group.
category: Fostering Welcoming School Climates for All Students

activity: Conducted robocalls to families in both English and Spanish to remind them to apply
description: The DOE targets families who did not apply through admissions using both English and Spanish.
category: Streamlining and increasing access for families to learn about school options and apply

activity: Finalized plans to open pre-K Main Round later and for a longer period of time, as well as introduce late application
description: Given feedback from the DOE's partners on the students in temporary housing initiative that the application was opened too early and closed too quickly, the DOE finalized plans to open the pre-Kindergarten application later and for a longer period of time. Additionally, the DOE will implement a "Late Application", which will eliminate "dead time" in between Rounds 1 and 2 when interested families do not have an action step available to them.
category: Simplifying Admissions Methods and Processes

activity: Public engagement process to increase school diversity in Community School District 15
description: The DOE is partnering with WXY Studio, a public engagement firm, and Community School District 15 to implement a public engagement process to foster school diversity in Community School District 15.
category: Equity & Excellence for All

activity: Piloted Family English Initiative
description: The DOE piloted the Family English Initiative in 6 schools to provide two-generation learning to students in Kindergarten through 2nd grade and their family members to learn English. Lessons were scaffolded around the best ways to support the learning of elementary students.
target_population: Spanish speaking and Chinese speaking families in Districts 7,8, and 25, and 31.
category: Fostering Welcoming School Climates for All Students

activity: Provided trainings for school staff working with Students in Temporary Housing (STH)
description: The DOE offered monthly professional development trainings to school principals and staff regarding specific rights, needs, expectations and how best to accommodate and collaborate on the needs of STH. Trainings were targeted primarily in the Brooklyn, as well as some districts across other boroughs.
category: Improving Efforts to Support Students in Temporary Housing

activity: Conducted additional outreach to students and families through 4410s, CPSEs, and the Turning 5 process for all elementary admissions processes
description: The Committees on Special Education (CSEs) and Committees on Pre School Special Education (CPSEs) work with families of students with disabilities, while 4410 programs are the primary providers of pre-Kindergarten special education programs and services. The DOE distributed directories to these sites and conducted outreach to encourage their participation in elementary admissions processes. Additionally, outreach was conducted to families participating in the Turning 5 process to encourage families to apply to kindergarten and submit a Gifted & Talented test registration.
category: Streamlining and increasing access for families to learn about school options and apply

activity: Support transition of students returning from court-ordered settings
description: In order to fully support and promote the transition of students returning from court-ordered settings, the DOE and the New York State Office of Children & Family Services (OCFS) are renewing their partnership and improving communication and data-sharing. The DOE and OCFS have developed an inter-agency transition team to improve communication and provide a more proactive, seamless transition as students re-enter DOE schools.
category: Streamlining and increasing access for families to learn about school options and apply

activity: Specialized High Schools Diversity Initiative -  Improve school climate at the Specialized High Schools to create more welcoming school cultures for diverse learners
description: In 2016-17, the DOE contracted with Ramapo for Children who conducted a School Culture and Climate Walkthrough at each of the 8 testing Specialized High Schools to assess the culture and climate of the school, including community values and expectations, relationships between adults and students, safety in the environment, and alignment of behavioral expectations across classrooms, shared spaces and transitions. The DOE is reviewing the results of the assessment and its potential impact on each school.
category: Improving Diversity at the Specialized High Schools

activity: Improved HS Admissions experience for students with accessibility needs
description: The DOE launched a pilot program in the fall of 2016 to assist a cohort of eighth-grade students and their families in identifying and applying to high schools that align with their accessibility needs. Findings from the pilot program are being used to build capacity at middle schools, high schools, and in the field offices so that students with accessibility needs are guided through the high school admissions process and high schools are prepared to welcome all students.
category: Streamlining and increasing access for families to learn about school options and apply

activity: Released diversity plan to facilitate more diverse and inclusive schools and programs
description: In June 2017, the DOE released Equity and Excellence for All: Diversity in New York City Public Schools. The release of this diversity plan is the next step in the City’s ongoing work to increase school diversity. It represents a critical milestone in the City’s Equity and Excellence for All agenda, and begins to lay out an approach to increasing diversity in the school system. The plan sets specific initial goals for making schools more diverse and inclusive that will be reported on annually. This includes 12 proposals to address policies and practices that pose challenges to school diversity; this report is organized in a way that aligns each activity to one of these proposals.
category: Equity & Excellence for All

activity: Held LGBT Inclusive Curriculum Conference
description: The DOE held an LGBT Inclusive Curriculum Conference, which brought together over 150 teachers across subjects, grade levels, and geography, to learn how to incorporate LGBT content into their curricula.
category: Fostering Welcoming School Climates for All Students
